knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Tsirizani_2024_darunavir"))$reference`
* Description (final model): `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Tsirizani_2024_darunavir"))$description`
* Description (supplementary AAG-binding model): `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Tsirizani_2024_darunavir_aagbinding"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1093/jac/dkae319> (open access, PMC11531812)

Tsirizani 2024 reports two fits to the same CHAPAS-4 darunavir data. The
final model (Table 3), packaged as `Tsirizani_2024_darunavir`, lets plasma
alpha-1-acid glycoprotein (AAG) lower apparent clearance directly. A
semi-mechanistic alternative (Supplementary Table 1 and Supplementary
Figure 2), packaged as `Tsirizani_2024_darunavir_aagbinding`, instead binds
darunavir saturably to AAG and clears only the free drug; it fitted better
(dOFV = 11) but the authors kept the simpler model for parsimony and
usability. Both are shipped so that the binding description can be used where
unbound exposure matters.

The companion ritonavir model from the same trial is
`Tsirizani_2025_ritonavir`.

# Population

Fifty-nine children aged 3.8-14.7 years (median 10.9) weighing 14.5-47.0 kg
(median 26.0), 55.9% female, from Zambia, Uganda and Zimbabwe, were randomised
to the darunavir/ritonavir arm of CHAPAS-4 after failing first-line
abacavir- or zidovudine-based ART (Table 1). Darunavir/ritonavir was given
once daily by weight band: 600/100 mg at 14-24.9 kg and 800/100 mg at 25 kg or
more (17.0-41.4 mg/kg darunavir). The NRTI backbone was tenofovir
alafenamide/emtricitabine (N = 34), abacavir/lamivudine (N = 12) or
zidovudine/lamivudine (N = 13). Median AAG was 0.7 g/L (0.3-1.9). Intensive
steady-state sampling at week 6 followed a witnessed dose taken with
breakfast, at pre-dose and 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 12 and 24 h (plus 0.5 h in the TAF
arm); 491 darunavir concentrations were analysed in NONMEM 7.5.1 with FOCE-I.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Tsirizani_2024_darunavir")()$population`.

# Typical-value checks

Two deterministic identities pin the encoding before any cohort is drawn.
Because the transit chain delivers the dose through a closed-form input
(`podo()` / `tad()`), the first check confirms the whole bioavailable dose
reaches the system: for the final model, a single dose must give
AUC(0-inf) = Dose / CL. For the binding model, only free drug is cleared, so at
steady state the free AUC over one interval must equal Dose / CLint.

```{r typical-checks}
mod_final <- readModelDb("Tsirizani_2024_darunavir")
mod_bind <- readModelDb("Tsirizani_2024_darunavir_aagbinding")

grid_sd <- seq(0, 480, by = 0.1)
ev_sd <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  data.frame(id = 1L, time = 0, evid = 1L, amt = 800, cmt = "depot"),
  data.frame(id = 1L, time = grid_sd, evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = "central")
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(WT = 26, AAG = 0.66, OCC = 2L)

trap <- function(t, y) sum(diff(t) * (head(y, -1) + tail(y, -1)) / 2)

sd_final <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod_final), ev_sd,
                            rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12) |>
  as.data.frame()
auc_sd <- trap(sd_final$time, sd_final$Cc)
cl_typ <- 8.05
c(AUC_sim = auc_sd, Dose_over_CL = 800 / cl_typ)
stopifnot(max(sd_final$Cc) > 1, abs(auc_sd / (800 / cl_typ) - 1) < 0.005)

# Steady state (7 daily doses), binding model: free AUC over the last
# interval x CLint = Dose.
ev_ss <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  data.frame(id = 1L, time = seq(0, 144, by = 24), evid = 1L, amt = 800,
             cmt = "depot"),
  data.frame(id = 1L, time = seq(144, 168, by = 0.05), evid = 0L, amt = 0,
             cmt = "central")
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(WT = 26, AAG = 0.7, OCC = 2L) |>
  dplyr::arrange(time, dplyr::desc(evid))

ss_bind <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod_bind), ev_ss,
                           rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12) |>
  as.data.frame()
# Seven daily doses leave the slow free-drug peripheral pool short of full
# accumulation, so solve a long run-in instead for the free-drug balance.
ev_ss_long <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  data.frame(id = 1L, time = seq(0, 24 * 59, by = 24), evid = 1L, amt = 800,
             cmt = "depot"),
  data.frame(id = 1L, time = seq(24 * 59, 24 * 60, by = 0.05), evid = 0L,
             amt = 0, cmt = "central")
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(WT = 26, AAG = 0.7, OCC = 2L) |>
  dplyr::arrange(time, dplyr::desc(evid))
ss_bind_long <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod_bind), ev_ss_long,
                                rtol = 1e-10, atol = 1e-12) |>
  as.data.frame()
auc_free <- trap(ss_bind_long$time, ss_bind_long$Cu)
c(CLint_x_AUCfree = 97.7 * auc_free, Dose = 800)
stopifnot(abs(97.7 * auc_free / 800 - 1) < 0.01)
```

Both identities hold. The binding model predicts an unbound fraction of
`r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * min(ss_bind$Cu / ss_bind$Cc))`-`r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * max(ss_bind$Cu / ss_bind$Cc))`%
over a steady-state interval at the median AAG, falling as total
concentration falls because binding is saturable.

```{r typical-profiles, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
ev_ss_typ <- ev_ss |>
  dplyr::mutate(AAG = 0.66)
ss_final <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod_final), ev_ss_typ) |>
  as.data.frame()
dplyr::bind_rows(
  dplyr::transmute(ss_final, model = "Final (Table 3)", tad = time - 144, Cc),
  dplyr::transmute(ss_bind, model = "AAG binding (Supplementary Table 1)",
                   tad = time - 144, Cc)
) |>
  ggplot(aes(tad, Cc, colour = model)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  labs(x = "Time after dose (h)", y = "Total darunavir (mg/L)", colour = NULL,
       title = "Typical 26 kg child, 800/100 mg once daily, steady state") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

The two fits describe nearly the same total-concentration profile for a
typical child, as expected for two models fitted to the same data.

# Virtual cohort

The paper's simulations (Figure 4) used a representative virtual population of
100,000 children dosed by weight band. Here each of the five Figure 4 arms
gets 100 children. Weight is drawn uniformly within the band (the upper band
capped at the observed maximum of 47 kg); AAG is drawn log-normally around the
0.7 g/L median with a log-scale SD of 0.35, clamped to the observed 0.3-1.9
g/L. Each child takes seven daily doses; the first six are occasion 1 and the
seventh, witnessed dose and its 24 h profile are occasion 2.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(20241101)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20241101)

arms <- tibble::tribble(
  ~arm,                       ~band,       ~wt_lo, ~wt_hi, ~dose,
  "14-19.9 kg, 600 mg",       "14-19.9",   14.5,   19.9,   600,
  "20-24.9 kg, 600 mg",       "20-24.9",   20,     24.9,   600,
  "25-34.9 kg, 600 mg (WHO)", "25-34.9",   25,     34.9,   600,
  "25-34.9 kg, 800 mg",       "25-34.9",   25,     34.9,   800,
  ">=35 kg, 800 mg",          ">=35",      35,     47,     800
)
n_per_arm <- 100L

cohort <- arms |>
  dplyr::mutate(arm_i = dplyr::row_number()) |>
  tidyr::uncount(n_per_arm) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    id = dplyr::row_number(),
    WT = stats::runif(dplyr::n(), wt_lo, wt_hi),
    AAG = pmin(pmax(stats::rlnorm(dplyr::n(), log(0.7), 0.35), 0.3), 1.9)
  )

dose_times <- seq(0, 144, by = 24)
obs_tad <- seq(0, 24, by = 0.5)

events <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  tidyr::expand_grid(cohort, time = dose_times) |>
    dplyr::mutate(evid = 1L, amt = dose, cmt = "depot",
                  OCC = ifelse(time < 144, 1L, 2L)),
  tidyr::expand_grid(cohort, time = 144 + obs_tad) |>
    dplyr::mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = "central", OCC = 2L)
) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, evid, amt, cmt, WT, AAG, OCC, arm, band) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))

stopifnot(
  !anyDuplicated(unique(events[, c("id", "time", "evid")])),
  max(table(cohort$arm)) <= 200
)
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_final, events = events,
                       keep = c("arm", "band", "WT", "AAG")) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  dplyr::mutate(tad = time - 144)
sim_bind <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_bind, events = events,
                            keep = c("arm", "band", "WT", "AAG")) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  dplyr::mutate(tad = time - 144)

stopifnot(
  all(is.finite(sim$Cc)), all(is.finite(sim_bind$Cc)),
  max(sim$Cc) > 1, max(sim_bind$Cc) > 1
)
```

# Replicate published figures

## Figure 1: median steady-state profiles by weight band

```{r figure-1, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5}
# Approximate medians of the 'Total' curve, read by the maintainers from
# Figure 1 of Tsirizani 2024 (observed data, all children).
fig1_total <- tibble::tibble(
  tad = c(0, 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24),
  Cc = c(1.4, 4.2, 6.2, 8.5, 7.0, 5.0, 3.1, 2.0)
)

sim |>
  dplyr::filter(arm != "25-34.9 kg, 600 mg (WHO)") |>
  dplyr::group_by(band, tad) |>
  dplyr::summarise(Cc = stats::median(Cc), .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(tad, Cc, colour = band)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(data = fig1_total, aes(tad, Cc), inherit.aes = FALSE,
             shape = 16, size = 2.5) +
  labs(x = "Time after dose (h)", y = "Median darunavir (mg/L)",
       colour = "Weight band (kg)",
       caption = paste("Lines: simulated medians, CHAPAS-4 dosing.",
                       "Points: observed total medians read from Figure 1.")) +
  theme_bw()
```

Replicates Figure 1 of Tsirizani 2024. The simulated medians peak at about
7-11 mg/L at 3-4 h, highest in the lightest band, and decline to 1.5-2 mg/L
at 24 h, as observed.

## Figure 4: simulated exposure by weight band

```{r figure-4-data}
exposure <- function(s, model) {
  s |>
    dplyr::group_by(id, arm, band) |>
    dplyr::summarise(
      AUC = trap(tad, Cc),
      Cmax = max(Cc),
      Ctrough = Cc[tad == 24],
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    dplyr::mutate(model = model)
}
expo <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  exposure(sim, "Final (Table 3)"),
  exposure(sim_bind, "AAG binding (Supplementary Table 1)")
)

# Medians read by the maintainers from the box plots of Figure 4.
fig4 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~arm,                       ~AUC, ~Cmax, ~Ctrough,
  "14-19.9 kg, 600 mg",       110,  10.5,  1.85,
  "20-24.9 kg, 600 mg",        88,   8.3,  1.55,
  "25-34.9 kg, 600 mg (WHO)",  71,   6.6,  1.35,
  "25-34.9 kg, 800 mg",        97,   8.8,  1.75,
  ">=35 kg, 800 mg",           77,   6.8,  1.45
)
```

```{r figure-4, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4.5}
expo_long <- expo |>
  dplyr::filter(model == "Final (Table 3)") |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(AUC, Cmax, Ctrough), names_to = "metric")
fig4_long <- fig4 |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(AUC, Cmax, Ctrough), names_to = "metric")
box_stats <- expo_long |>
  dplyr::group_by(arm, metric) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    ymin = stats::quantile(value, 0.025), lower = stats::quantile(value, 0.25),
    middle = stats::median(value), upper = stats::quantile(value, 0.75),
    ymax = stats::quantile(value, 0.975), .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(arm = factor(arm, levels = arms$arm))

ggplot(box_stats, aes(x = arm)) +
  geom_boxplot(
    aes(ymin = ymin, lower = lower, middle = middle, upper = upper, ymax = ymax),
    stat = "identity", fill = "lightblue"
  ) +
  geom_point(data = dplyr::mutate(fig4_long, arm = factor(arm, levels = arms$arm)),
             aes(arm, value), colour = "red", shape = 18, size = 3) +
  facet_wrap(~metric, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "AUC0-24 (mg*h/L) / Cmax, Ctrough (mg/L)",
       caption = paste("Boxes: IQR, whiskers 2.5th-97.5th percentile (final model).",
                       "Red diamonds: medians read from Figure 4.")) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

Replicates Figure 4 of Tsirizani 2024.

```{r figure-4-table}
fig4_cmp <- expo |>
  dplyr::group_by(model, arm) |>
  dplyr::summarise(dplyr::across(c(AUC, Cmax, Ctrough), stats::median),
                   .groups = "drop") |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(AUC, Cmax, Ctrough), names_to = "metric",
                      values_to = "simulated") |>
  dplyr::inner_join(fig4_long, by = c("arm", "metric")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (simulated / value - 1))

fig4_cmp |>
  dplyr::mutate(arm = factor(arm, levels = arms$arm)) |>
  dplyr::arrange(model, metric, arm) |>
  dplyr::rename("Model" = model, "Arm" = arm, "Metric" = metric,
                "Simulated median" = simulated, "Figure 4 median" = value,
                "% difference" = pct_diff) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2,
               caption = "Simulated cohort medians versus Figure 4 medians.")

final_auc <- dplyr::filter(fig4_cmp, model == "Final (Table 3)", metric == "AUC")
stopifnot(
  # The whole-cohort AUC centre: a mis-transcribed clearance or dose moves
  # every arm together by tens of percent.
  abs(stats::median(final_auc$pct_diff)) < 15,
  # Per-arm envelope, wide enough for 100-child cohort medians, the
  # within-band weight assumption and reading medians off a box plot.
  all(abs(final_auc$pct_diff) < 30)
)
```

The final model reproduces the Figure 4 pattern: the lightest band on 600 mg
has the highest exposure, the WHO 600 mg dose in the 25-34.9 kg band gives the
lowest, and the CHAPAS-4 800 mg dose in that band sits above the adult median
AUC of 69.4 mg*h/L. The supplementary binding model gives similar total
exposures.

# PKNCA validation

PKNCA is run on the final-model cohort over the steady-state interval, using
only the study's sampling times (0, 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 12 and 24 h), because the
published NCA used those samples. Only the CHAPAS-4 arms are compared.

```{r pknca}
paper_times <- c(0, 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24)
nca_conc <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc), tad %in% paper_times,
                arm != "25-34.9 kg, 600 mg (WHO)") |>
  dplyr::select(id, band, tad, Cc)
nca_dose <- cohort |>
  dplyr::filter(arm != "25-34.9 kg, 600 mg (WHO)") |>
  dplyr::transmute(id, band, tad = 0, amt = dose)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_conc, Cc ~ tad | band + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(nca_dose, amt ~ tad | band + id)
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = 24, auclast = TRUE, cmax = TRUE,
                        cmin = TRUE)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj,
                                          intervals = intervals))
```

## Comparison against published NCA

The paper's NCA (Table 2, Supplementary Table 3) reports geometric means of
observed concentrations; the comparison table below reports simulated medians,
which for these log-normally distributed exposures are close to geometric
means. The trough is the 24 h concentration (`cmin` over a steady-state
interval).

```{r nca-compare}
published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~band,      ~auclast, ~cmax, ~cmin,
  "14-19.9",   98.5,     9.6,   1.4,
  "20-24.9",   94.7,     9.3,   1.3,
  "25-34.9",  100.4,     9.8,   1.7,
  ">=35",      82.3,     7.5,   1.8
)

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = published,
  by = "band",
  params = c("auclast", "cmax", "cmin"),
  units = c(auclast = "mg*h/L", cmax = "mg/L", cmin = "mg/L"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(
  cmp,
  caption = paste("Simulated steady-state NCA (median) versus Supplementary",
                  "Table 3 geometric means by weight band.",
                  "* differs by more than 20%.")
)

nca_auc <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast")
pooled_gm <- exp(mean(log(nca_auc$PPORRES)))
c(simulated_pooled_GM_AUC = pooled_gm, Table2_GM_AUC = 94.3)
stopifnot(abs(pooled_gm / 94.3 - 1) < 0.2)
```

The pooled geometric-mean AUC(0-24) agrees with the observed 94.3 mg*h/L of
Table 2, and AUC and Cmax agree within 15% in every band. The trough in the
heaviest band falls furthest from the observed value: the observed geometric
mean is 1.8 mg/L in 13 children whose NCA half-life was unusually long and
variable (13.4 h, 77% CV, Supplementary Table 3). The paper's own Figure 4
simulation puts the median trough for that band near 1.45 mg/L, below the
observed value too, so the gap is between the published model and that band's
observed data, not in the encoding.

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Variability scale.** Table 3 and Supplementary Table 1 give BSV and BOV as
  percentages without saying whether they are log-scale standard deviations or
  coefficients of variation. The maintainers read them as omega x 100
  (omega^2 = (pct/100)^2), the convention verified against the supplemental
  control stream of the same group's CHAPAS-4 ritonavir analysis
  (`Tsirizani_2025_ritonavir`). Reading them as CVs instead would shrink the
  60.8% MTT BOV variance from 0.370 to 0.315.
- **Occasions.** The paper says only that BOV was placed on the absorption
  parameters. Each child had one intensive PK day, so the occasions are taken
  to be the unwitnessed doses before the PK day (OCC = 1) and the witnessed
  PK-day dose (OCC = 2), as in the ritonavir analysis, with one shared
  variance per parameter. The 2.14-fold BOV inflation estimated for unwitnessed
  ritonavir doses is not part of this darunavir model.
- **Transit chain.** The paper cites Savic 2007 for the transit compartments;
  the model uses that parameterisation, `ktr = (NN + 1) / MTT`, with the
  chain feeding an absorption compartment drained at `ka` (Supplementary
  Figure 2). The non-integer NN is implemented with the closed-form gamma
  input, which is exact for daily dosing because the chain empties within a
  few hours.
- **AAG reference.** The clearance equation centres AAG at 0.66 g/L (Table 3
  footnote c) while the binding model centres Bmax at 0.7 g/L (Supplementary
  Table 1 footnote), the rounded Table 1 median. Both are used as printed.
- **Binding-model structure.** Supplementary Figure 2 shows free darunavir
  exchanging with the peripheral compartment and being cleared; the model
  therefore treats the peripheral compartment as holding free drug, with
  central-to-peripheral flux `Q * Cfree` and return flux `Q * Aperipheral /
  Vp`. Binding is instantaneous and solved in closed form from the total
  concentration. Several binding-model parameters (CLint, Q, V2, NN, Kd, Bmax)
  are printed without a confidence interval; the Discussion states they were
  estimated with priors from Schalkwijk et al., so they are not marked as
  fixed.
- **Virtual cohort.** Weight is uniform within each band and AAG log-normal
  (median 0.7 g/L, log-SD 0.35, clamped to 0.3-1.9 g/L); the paper's
  100,000-child simulation population is not described further. The Figure 1
  and Figure 4 medians were read from the published images by the maintainers
  and are approximate.
- **NRTI backbone, age and ritonavir exposure** had no significant effect and
  are not in either model.
